Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment — Saturday is a light-wind day under a high-pressure ridge, with weak thermals and a lot of thin high cloud that thins out in the afternoon. Rainbow Ridge is the clear pick, with steady east wind, the day's best thermals and some ridge lift. Hallelujah has a short midday thermal window, and most other sites offer sled rides at best. NWS Reno expects a strong storm to bring high winds starting Sunday, so treat Saturday as the last calm day before the change.

Site Breakdown

Rainbow Ridge Favorable — Steady launch-aligned east wind all afternoon combines with the day's strongest thermals and building ridge lift.
Window: 11am–3pm
Thermal strength is 210–261 ft/min from 11am to 2pm and peaks around 12–1pm, with the thermal top at 1,330–1,712 ft above ground. Wind is 4–9 mph from 90–101°, well aligned. Ridge lift builds from +67 ft/min at 11am to +163 ft/min at 3pm. That is not enough on its own to stay up, so plan on mixing it with thermals. Thermals fade after 3pm, but wind stays aligned at 5–8 mph until 4pm. Thermal roughness (turbulence, sigma-w) is mild at 0.4 m/s.

Not recommended today (8) — click a row for details

Hallelujah Marginal — Thermals are usable, but the wind is launch-aligned only from about 11am to 1pm before swinging to a southeast tailwind.
Window: 11am–1pm
Thermal strength is 170–224 ft/min in the window and peaks at 247 ft/min around 1pm, with the thermal top rising from 1,062 to 1,706 ft above ground (up to 2,118 ft by 1pm). Wind is a light 2–3 mph from 308–316° late morning. From 1pm it turns to come from 107–136°, which is behind launch, and builds to 8–10 mph by 3–4pm, so evening soaring is not on. This run improved from the previous one: thermals are stronger and cloud cover is lower.
Slide Mountain Marginal — Sled ride only: launch wind is light and aligned in the morning, but there are no thermals at all.
Window: 9am–11am
Thermal strength is 0 ft/min all day. Launch wind is 2–3 mph from 162–188° in the morning, and the model shows 2–5 mph at 1,000 ft above launch. Wind 3,000 ft above launch is much stronger, 22–29 mph from the northwest, until noon. Launch is cold at 32–43 °F. The share of hours with aligned light wind improved from 0% to 28% since the previous run.
Peavine Mountain Marginal — Sled ride only, with light aligned wind from late morning to early afternoon and almost no thermals.
Window: 11am–1pm
Thermal strength peaks at 46 ft/min, so this is not soarable. Launch wind is 4–6 mph from 155–204°, within the preferred range. Wind 3,000 ft above launch is 25–29 mph from the northwest through noon, though it is only 3–5 mph at 1,000 ft above launch, so stay low and do not try to climb out. Launch is cool at 34–46 °F.
Duck Hill Marginal — Morning north-northwest wind is aligned and gives some ridge lift, but too little to soar and with no thermals.
Window: 8am–11am
Wind is 4–6 mph from 329–11° in the morning. Ridge lift is +162 ft/min at 8am and drops to +78 by 10am, short of the roughly 200 ft/min needed to stay up, so expect sled rides. Thermal strength is essentially zero. Afternoon wind turns light from 140–170°, behind launch, so evening soaring is not expected.
Kingsbury grade Unfavorable — Light north wind blows from behind or across this southeast-facing launch all day, and thermals are too weak to stay up in.
Thermal strength (w*) peaks at only 174 ft/min around 12pm, below a paraglider's sink rate of about 200 ft/min. The thermal top (height of the mixed layer, PBLH) reaches only 945 ft above ground (AGL). Wind is 2–4 mph from 340–30°, well off the preferred 104°. Stable air flows around most of the slope below launch, so expect little ridge lift.
McClellan Unfavorable — Wind is aligned for about one hour near noon and is otherwise a north tailwind or an east crosswind, with almost no thermals.
Peak thermal strength is only 57 ft/min at 12pm. At 12pm the wind is 4 mph from 134°, which is acceptable for a sled ride. Before that it is 4–5 mph from 335–352°, and after that it is 6 mph from 90–99°, which is cross to the southwest launch.
West McClellan Unfavorable — Wind never comes from the west, and launch sits on the downwind side, with sinking air all afternoon.
Wind is from the northeast in the morning, then 6–8 mph from 137–150° in the afternoon, against a preferred 270°. Ridge lift is negative, -37 to -66 ft/min, from noon on. Peak thermal strength is only 35 ft/min.
Daydreams Unfavorable — Morning wind comes from the east-northeast, behind this southwest launch, and the afternoon is calm with no thermals.
Wind is 3–6 mph from 52–85° until 1pm, then 0–2 mph. Peak thermal strength is only 27 ft/min. The evening wind at 4pm is 2 mph from 293°, outside the preferred direction and too light for evening soaring.

Hazards

  • Strong wind aloft over high launches: Wind 3,000 ft above the Slide Mountain and Peavine launches is 22–29 mph from the northwest until noon, and NWS Reno reports Sierra ridge gusts of 40–50 mph easing through the morning. Crest-level wind of 13–20 knots from the northwest falls to 2 knots by 4pm. That is below the strength and outside the direction that usually brings lee-side rotor to Reno, so lee-side risk is unclear but not supported by the model.
  • Model wind confidence at ridge height: In the early hours of this run, the model read 50–58 mph at the Slide Mountain summit station against an observed 13–26 mph, with one gust to 41 mph. That suggests the model may be overstating wind aloft. These are start-up hours and only weak evidence, but treat the upper-wind numbers with some caution.
  • Morning haze and fog: NWS Reno mentions an inversion that may reduce slant visibility around Reno, Carson City and Minden until about 10am Saturday, and patchy freezing fog at Truckee until about 7–8am. Visibility is not modeled here.
  • Storm and wind shear arriving Saturday night: NWS Reno expects southwest winds of up to 40 knots near 10,000 ft, with turbulence and low-level wind shear (LLWS) starting late Saturday evening, after the flying window. Strong winds, Lake Wind Advisories and rain or snow follow Sunday. Pack up by sunset Saturday and do not plan on flying Sunday.
